Regio- and Stereoselective Synthesis of Highly Functionalized
Tetrasubstituted Ole ﬁns by Iodine-Mediated Iodofunctionalization
of Ferrocene-Containing Allenylphosphonates
Le Guo, Yanpeng Gao, Zishuo Wang, Zhi Li, Yingjie Zhang, Haidong Wang, Xihui Chen, Zhenbo Gong,
and Shufeng Chen *
Cite This: J. Org. Chem. 2020, 85, 7358 −7367 Read Online
ACCESS Metrics & More Article Recommendations *sı Supporting Information
ABSTRACT: An iodine-mediated iodofunctionalization of ferro-
cene-containing allenylphosphonates with various carboxylic acids,
alcohols, and phenols has been established, a ﬀording a series of
highly functionalized tetrasubstituted alkenylphosphonate deriva-
tives with high regio- and stereoselectivities in moderate to good
yields. This approach provides an opportunity to the useful but not
readily available tetrasubstituted ole ﬁns. The stereoselectivity of the
reaction may be controlled by the neighboring group participation
of the oxygen atom of the phosphate group.
■ INTRODUCTION
The alkene moiety is among the most pervasive functional
groups present in various organic frameworks. In this regard,
tetrasubstituted ole ﬁns are compelling structural motifs found
in many natural products, 1 pharmaceutical,2 and organic
functional materials. 3 Moreover, they are also versatile
intermediates for complex molecule syntheses as they are
subjects of a wide range of transformations.
4 Therefore,
enormous attention has been paid to their high selective and
functionalized synthesis.
5 Among various approaches, the
electrophilic addition of substituted allenes appears to be
most e ﬃcient and modular, providing an interesting case of
tetrasubstituted ole ﬁnf o r m a t i o n .
6 However, due to the
presence of two C C bonds, controlling regioselectivity as
well as stereoselectivity of the reaction to the preparation of
geometrically de ﬁned tetrasubstituted ole ﬁns is still a
formidable challenge. In addition, the application of the
aforementioned methods to the syntheses of tetrasubstituted
oleﬁns is often limited in the mono- or disubstituted allenes.
Therefore, the development of an e ﬃcient method for the
construction of diverse functionalized tetrasubstituted alkenes
from congested trisubstituted allenes remains highly sought
after.
On the other hand, the alkenylphosphonate compound
(Figure 1 ), which has been applied to pharmaceuticals and
agrochemicals as well as various transformations to a ﬀord other
functional molecules, is an attractive target.
7 Therefore,
signiﬁcant e ﬀorts have been devoted to the preparation of
this type of compound. Traditionally, Wittig −Horner and
transition-metal catalyzed Michaelis −Arbuzov reactions were
the main synthetic methods for the preparation of these
alkenylphosphonates with de ﬁned stereochemistry.
8 Moreover,
Heck-type reactions were also successfully applied in the
synthesis of alkenylphosphonates using various coupling
partners.
9 However, some of these methods su ﬀer from
drawbacks such as functional group tolerance, relatively harsh
reaction conditions, and the use of di ﬃcult-to-access starting
materials. In addition, transition-metal-catalyzed hydrophos-
phorylation of alkynes has become an attractive way to
synthesize vinylphosphonates,
10 but in most cases only
terminal alkynes are e ﬀective. Recently, a palladium-catalyzed
coupling reaction of α-diazo or N-tosylhydrazone phospho-
nates with benzyl or allyl halides for the stereoselective
syntheses of trisubstituted vinylphosphonates has been
reported by Wang and co-workers.
11 However, methods to
synthesize diverse functionalized tetrasubstituted alkenyl-
phosphonates are still limited.
12 We envisioned that the

electrophilic addition of trisubstituted allenylphosphonates
may provide an e ﬃcient route to the preparation of
tetrasubstituted alkenylphosphonates despite the existing
challenge of controlling reactivity as well as selectivity of the
reaction. Therefore, in continuation of our interest in the
functionalization of allenes,
13 herein we report an iodine-
mediated highly regio- and stereoselective iodofunctionaliza-
tion reaction of allenylphosphonates with a series of alcohols,
phenols, and carboxylic acids, which provides a straightforward
and convenient route to not readily available functionalized
tetrasubstituted alkenylphosphonate compounds with excellent
selectivity ( Scheme 1 ).
■ RESULTS AND DISCUSSION
With this idea in mind, the electrophilic addition of
allenylphosphonate 1a with benzoic acid 2a and I 2 was ﬁrst
chosen as the model reaction to optimize the reaction
conditions ( Table 1 ). Gratifyingly, the desired product ( E)-
3a was obtained in a 45% yield as the only stereoisomer when
the reaction was carried out in tetrahydrofuran (THF) at room
temperature (r.t.) for 1 h in the presence of 1 equiv of NaOH
in an air atmosphere ( Table 1, entry 1). Other solvents, such as
CH
3CN, CH3OH, toluene, and dioxane, furnished the desired
product in 9, 19, 35, 42% yields, respectively ( Table 1 , entries
2−5). Similarly, dichloromethane (DCM) was also con ﬁrmed
to be suitable for this transformation, furnishing ( E)-3a in a
slightly higher yield ( Table 1 , entry 6). Subsequently, we
carefully examined the e ﬀect of the base on this electrophilic
addition reaction. KOH and Cs 2CO3 were found to be less
eﬃcient (Table 1, entries 7 and 8). The reaction with t-BuOLi
provided ( E)-3a in a high isolated yield ( Table 1 , entry 9).
Switching t-BuOLi to LiOH did not increase the yield of the
product ( Table 1 , entry 10). Only a trace amount of ( E)-3a
was detected when the reaction proceeded with an organic
base ( Table 1 , entry 11). Increasing the reaction temperature
led to a drop in the yield ( Table 1, entry 12). Finally, the ratio
of substrates was examined, and it was found that a 1a/2a/
iodine/base ratio of 1.0:2.0:1.0:1.0 led to the highest yield of
the desired product ( Table 1 , entry 13). Therefore, the
conditions in entry 13 ( Table 1) were identi ﬁed as the optimal
conditions. It should be noted that the reaction proceeded with
high regio- and stereoselectivities with the double bond having
E conﬁguration. The exact structure of ( E)-3a was further
unambiguously elucidated by X-ray di ﬀraction analysis of the
single crystal.
14
With the optimized reaction conditions in hand, we then
proceeded to study the scope of the current iodofunctionaliza-
tion reaction using various allenylphosphonates and carboxylic
acids as the substrates, and the experimental data are shown in
Scheme 2 . Most aromatic acids worked well with allenyl-
phosphonate 1a to give ferrocene-containing tetrasubstituted
alkenylphosphonates 3a−g in moderate to good yields. It was
found that various substituents on the phenyl ring of benzoic
acids, such as ﬂuoro, chloro, bromo, iodo, and methoxy, were
well-tolerated under optimal conditions. Unfortunately, the
electron-withdrawing group with 4-CN attached to the phenyl
ring was proved to be fruitless, probably due to the strong
electronic e ﬀect ( 3h). Moreover, heteroaryl species such as β-
indoleacetic acid as substrate failed to a ﬀord any corresponding
products ( 3i). Furthermore, two aliphatic acids were also
tested and gave the corresponding products 3j and 3k in 46
and 35% yields, respectively. Our next objective was to check
the scope of trisubstituted allenylphosphonate substrates.
Delightfully, with regard to the R
1 group of the allenes,
diﬀerent substituents on the phenyl ring were all suitable for
this transformation, a ﬀording the tetrasubstituted alkenyl-
phosphonate products in good to high yields ( 3l−s). Notably,
a free hydroxyl group could survive well and the reaction
proceeded smoothly to give alkenylphosphonate product 3p in
an 82% yield. Moreover, except for aromatic ring groups, the
alkyl substituent could also be introduced to the ole ﬁn
product, albeit with a slightly lower yield ( 3t). Finally, a gram-
scale experiment of 1a with 2a was carried out to examine the
scalability, and a 66% yield of 3a was obtained on the 2.5 mmol
scale under the standard conditions, validating that this
method is scalable.
The potential impact of this transformation would be
expanded if alcohols could be employed as nucleophilic
reagents for the reaction. Thus, to expand the scope of the
tetrasubstituted alkenylphosphonate formation reaction fur-
ther, diverse alcohols were employed as substrates under the

proved to be good substrates, providing the corresponding

products with satisfactory yields ( 5b−d). Moreover, second
alcohols were also suitable for this reaction, a ﬀording the
desired products 5e and 5f in 59 and 50% yields, respectively.
However, increasing the steric hindrance further by employing
a tertiary alcohol resulted in the alkenylphosphonate product
5g being obtained in a lower yield, probably because of the
steric hindrance e ﬀect. Finally, randomly selected three
trisubstituted allenylphosphonate compounds were subjected
to the reaction and furnished the corresponding products in
moderate to good yields as a single stereoisomer in each case
(5h−j).
Encouraged by the success in the application of alcohols, we
next turned our attention to expanding the substrate scope to
phenols. We found that under optimal reaction conditions, as
shown in Scheme 4, the iodine-mediated iodofunctionalization
of allenylphosphonate with phenols led to the formation of E-
tetrasubstituted alkenylphosphonates in moderate yields with
complete stereoselectivity. When an electron-donating sub-
stituent such as methyl group was introduced, the reaction
proceeded smoothly ( 7b), while tert-butyl group decreased the
reaction e ﬃciency ( 7c). In contrast, the desired product was
not formed when a strong electron-withdrawing group was
incorporated ( 7d). Moreover, halogen substituted phenols
were all e ﬃciently coupled to furnish the corresponding
products in moderate yields ( 7e−g). However, the ortho
substituent hampered the reaction and no desired product was
detected (7h). Finally, the reaction of 4-phenylphenol gave rise
to 7i in a 40% isolated yield.
The high regio- and stereoselectivity for ferrocene-
containing tetrasubstituted alkenylphosphonate formation
may be interpreted by the protocol shown in Scheme 5 .
Initially, the iodonium intermediate A was formed regiose-
lectively by the direct electrophilic addition of the relatively
electron-rich carbon−carbon double bond with I
2. Next, a ﬁve-
membered intermediate B was generated via the neighboring
group participation of the oxygen atom of the phosphate
group.
12b Finally, the oxygen nucleophile attacks at the α
position of the ferrocene group accompanied by cleavage of the
C−O bond, which a ﬀorded the highly stereoselective E-isomer
as the ﬁnal product.
■ CONCLUSIONS
We have developed a practical method for the construction of
useful tetrasubstituted alkenylphosphonates via iodine-medi-
ated electrophilic addition of ferrocene-containing allenyl-
phosphonates with various oxygen nucleophiles in high regio-
Scheme 3. Highly Regio- and Stereoselective Iodoalkoxylation of Allenylphosphonates with Various Alcohols a
aReactions were carried out with 0.20 mmol of 1, 0.40 mmol of 4, 0.20 mmol of iodine, 0.20 mmol of t-BuOLi in 3.0 mL of DCM at room
temperature. Yields of the isolated product after chromatography.

and stereoselectivity. The approach provided a series of highly
functionalized tetrasubstituted ole ﬁns in moderate to excellent
yields with good functional tolerance. It is believed that the
stereoselectivity of the reaction may be controlled by the
neighboring group participation of the oxygen atom of the
phosphate group. We are con ﬁdent that this protocol would
allow the synthesis of many highly substituted allenylphosph-
onate analogues.
■ EXPERIMENTAL SECTION
General Information. All commercially available reagents were
used directly without puri ﬁcation unless otherwise stated. All solvents
were puri ﬁed following standard procedures. For chromatography,
100−200 mesh silica gel (Qingdao, China) was employed. 1H and 13C
NMR spectra were recorded at 500 and 125 MHz, respectively.
Chemical shifts are reported in ppm using tetramethylsilane as
internal standard when CDCl 3 was used as solvent. IR spectra were
recorded on a Fourier transform infrared (FT-IR) instrument. The
high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS) analysis was obtained on
a quadrupole time-of- ﬂight (QTOF) mass spectrometer. Melting
points were determined with melting point apparatus and are
uncorrected. Allenylphosphonates 1 were prepared according to our
previously described procedures.
